newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The latest farmers' protests has brought ideological differences in ruling party PASOK again to the fore. Senior government members are among those who distanced themselves from the hardline stance espoused by the prime minister. The differences are expected to appear again when Parliament debates the bill on a uniform wage scale for civil servants and the bill on spending cutbacks.

--President Kostis Stephanopoulos yesterday called on Greeks to support Greece's European course, while the Communist Party of Greece jump-started its campaign for the government to hold a referendum on Maastricht.

--The defusion of the farmers' protests, combined with the news that January CPI inflation had fallen below 7.0 percent, boosted trading on the Athens bourse yesterday to new highs, with the general price index closing at over 1,200 points, the first time in six years.

--Yesterday's violence in Albania has set alarm bells ringing in Athens over fears of a new wave of illegal immigrants from the neighbouring country. The public order ministry is coordinating plans involving the army, coast guard and police across the northern border.

--The conclusions of an inquiry into the ramming of gunboat "Kostakos" last year by a passenger ferry off Samos - conducted by an expert appointed by the merchant marine ministry and the courts - has laid the blame squarely on the gunboat, in direct opposition to an earlier inquiry by the navy.
--Greece is the 'bad boy' of the European Union, cutting class in more than half of the 2,000 meetings called to take decisions on important issues.

--The government is facing enormous difficulty is dealing with the issue of making up for school lessons lost over the last four weeks of the teachers' strike. OLME, the high school teachers' union, has accused the education ministry of using threats to extend the school year as a tactic to pit students and parents against teachers. OLME looks set to recommend a fifth week to the strike at tomorrow's meeting.
--EU sources say the government will be obliged to take more revenue-gathering measures over the summer if it is to achieve convergence.

--Senior government officials who contributed to the government's information blitz for farmers over the weekend will get their due reward, according to a new plan promoted by ruling party PASOK Secretary Costas Skandalidis which foresees leading members taking a higher profile.
